findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a classifier (or a pre-pass detector) that recognises pandoc-generated inline Jira wiki markup in prose paragraphs (*bold*, _italic_, [label|url], {color:}...{color}) as already-rendered wiki and passes those units exactly, so the idempotency AC ('five-pass exact') is mechanically achievable.
evidence: Plan classifier 1 only catches 'units beginning h1.-h6., {code}, {noformat}, or {{' — inline constructs like *bold* or _italic_ in the BODY of a pandoc-generated paragraph do not begin with any of these prefixes.

Pandoc's Jira writer emits *text* for bold, _text_ for italic, {{text}} only for monospace, and [label|url] for links; of these only {{text}} would be caught by classifier 1 (starts with {{), the rest would re-enter pandoc.

Plan states: 'Existing wiki stays exact over repeated rendering' and AC: 'Existing wiki/noformat stays exact over five passes; idempotence tests.' — the mechanism does not deliver this guarantee for inline formatted prose paragraphs.
ABSENCE: the plan specifies no 'already rendered' detector, no Jira-inline-markup classifier, and no 'do not re-render if output looks like Jira wiki' guard.
findings.finding: The idempotency guarantee ('Existing wiki stays exact over repeated rendering') is mechanically unsound for inline Jira wiki markup emitted by pandoc's Jira writer in prose paragraphs. After the first pass, a paragraph may contain Jira-wiki inline constructs such as *bold*, _italic_, {{monospace}}, or [link|url]. On a second pass, these units fail all four classifiers (they don't start with h1.-h6., {code}, {noformat}, or {{; they aren't ASCII tables; they aren't HTML comments/tags; they don't contain regex-dangerous patterns) and are re-classified as remaining prose to be re-rendered by pandoc. Pandoc interprets *bold* as CommonMark emphasis and emits _bold_ (Jira italic), breaking convergence.
findings.location: Renderer contract section — 'Classify' rules 1–5; Acceptance Criteria — 'Existing wiki/noformat stays exact over five passes; idempotence tests.'
scenarios: A Markdown paragraph 'This is **bold** text.' is rendered by pandoc to 'This is *bold* text.' (Jira bold). On a second pass the unit reaches pandoc as CommonMark where *bold* is italic, yielding 'This is _bold_ text.' — a Jira-italic paragraph. Five-pass idempotency test would fail.

A Markdown paragraph with a link '[label](url)' is rendered by pandoc to '[label|url]'. On re-entry this passes no classifier and is re-sent to pandoc, which interprets [label|url] as plain text — the link is lost.
Any corpus fixture whose prose body contains Markdown emphasis or links will fail the idempotency AC once the first-pass output re-enters the renderer.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend classifier 1 to also pass units whose content matches a Jira-inline-markup heuristic (e.g. contains `*...*`, `_..._`, `[...|...]`, or `{color`). Alternatively, run a post-pandoc step that detects whether the output already round-trips through pandoc unchanged (convert back from jira→commonmark and check equivalence), and if not, cache the output as the fixed point.

It is unclear whether 'fallback class' refers to a Python logging record class, a sentinel exception class, a log message category string, or something else. The AC cannot be written unambiguously without knowing what artifact the test should assert against.
findings.location: Renderer contract — 'Conversion/preservation failure returns that unit with a content-free structured debug fallback class'; AC — 'Failure log names only fallback class; fallback test'
scenarios: Implementer emits a logger.debug() call with a custom class name; test author asserts on the log message string — different artifacts.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve the conflict between 'Wiki tests never importorskip' and 'core/BSD keeps identity fallback': either (a) add a platform-capability guard so wiki tests are skipped when pypandoc-binary is unavailable (e.g. mark the hard-import test with a `pytest.importorskip` or platform marker), or (b) document that BSD is explicitly excluded from the dev/test environment and update the portability statement accordingly.
evidence: 'Wiki tests never importorskip; dev installs wiki in project pytest lanes.'
'Binary support covers project Linux/macOS CI plus Windows wheels; core/BSD keeps identity fallback.'
'A non-skipping test hard-imports pypandoc, requires 3.6.1, then proves the jira writer with an exact heading conversion'

BSD is named as a supported platform in the plan itself and in the rebar support matrix; pypandoc-binary==1.15 does not publish BSD wheels, so `uv sync --extra wiki` would fail or have no effect on BSD.
findings.finding: The plan simultaneously requires 'Wiki tests never importorskip' (with a hard-import of pypandoc and a required pandoc 3.6.1 version assertion) and acknowledges 'core/BSD keeps identity fallback' because pypandoc-binary does not ship BSD wheels. On a BSD developer workstation where the wiki extra cannot be installed, the non-skipping hard-import tests will fail with an ImportError or a missing-wheel installation error, making the full test suite non-runnable on a supported platform.
findings.location: Dependency and CI section: 'Wiki tests never importorskip; dev installs wiki in project pytest lanes' and 'Binary support covers project Linux/macOS CI plus Windows wheels; core/BSD keeps identity fallback'
scenarios: BSD developer workstation: running `make test` after `uv sync --locked --extra wiki` either fails to install pypandoc-binary (no wheel for BSD) or hard-imports fail with ImportError in test_dc_real_pandoc_version, making the full test suite non-green on a supported platform that the plan explicitly acknowledges.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a `pytest.mark.skipif` or `pytest.importorskip` guard specifically on tests that hard-import pypandoc and require pandoc 3.6.1, conditioned on whether pypandoc-binary is installable on the current platform. The identity-fallback behavior can then be tested separately without requiring the binary. This preserves the 'never skip in CI' guarantee for Linux/macOS/Windows while allowing BSD developer workstations to run the suite.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define 'eligible safe unit' explicitly in the plan (e.g., 'a prose or heading unit dispatched to pandoc classifier 5, excluding locked blocks, tables, HTML/regex-pass-through, and already-wiki units') so the corpus script and coverage tests use the same denominator.
evidence: 'Body ratio = bodies with a changed eligible safe unit / 178. Character ratio = source characters in changed eligible units / source characters in all eligible units.'
'Records declare source, protected excerpts, and eligible safe units independently of renderer output.'
Renderer contract classifiers 1–4 all produce exact pass-through output (no change), making 'eligible' non-trivially different from 'all units' — but this exclusion is never stated.
findings.finding: The term 'eligible safe units' is central to the two corpus coverage metrics (body ratio and character ratio) but is never formally defined in the plan. The renderer contract does not label which classifier outputs are 'eligible', and the corpus section only says 'Records declare...eligible safe units independently of renderer output' without specifying the rule. An implementer must infer — likely 'units dispatched to pandoc (classifier 5)' — but this guess affects both the fixture generation script and the coverage tests in a load-bearing way.
findings.location: Corpus section (body ratio / character ratio definition); Acceptance Criteria — 'Rendered-body ratio >=0.90' and 'Rendered-character ratio >=0.95 over eligible source'
scenarios: scripts/build_dc_wiki_corpus.py author writes eligible_safe_units to include pass-through blocks, causing ratio denominator inflation and tests to fail unexpectedly.
test_dc_corpus_coverage.py author excludes too much or too little from the denominator, producing a metric that cannot be reproduced across implementations.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a one-sentence definition: 'An eligible safe unit is any blank-line-delimited block or list item classified into pandoc rendering (classifier 5); locked blocks, tables, HTML/regex-pass units, and pre-existing wiki units are ineligible.'

findings.finding: The arrow-to-Unicode mapping is stated only implicitly through ordering. The plan says 'Map arrows to ↔/→/←/⇒' and lists the ordered alternation as '<!--, -->, <->, ->, <-, =>' but never explicitly pairs each token with its output symbol. An implementer must infer the mapping by correspondence, which is error-prone for the two identity mappings (<!-- and --> map to themselves).
findings.location: Renderer contract — 'In safe units make one regex pass ordered <!--, -->, <->, ->, <-, =>. Map arrows to ↔/→/←/⇒; both HTML delimiters always map to themselves'

findings.suggested_fix: Replace the implicit correspondence with: 'Map <-> to ↔, -> to →, <- to ←, => to ⇒; both <!-- and --> map to themselves (identity).'
